newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia aims for 4-5 pct GDP growth in 1997-98 - PM.
newsitem.headline: Estonia aims for 4-5 pct GDP growth in 1997-98 - PM.

text.p: Estonian Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi said his government has approved a programme for the next two years which includes planned GDP growth of four to five percent and an inflation target of 10 to 14 percent.
The final version of the government policy document has not yet been released but Vaehi told a news conference on Tuesday that 1997, like 1996, would be a year of "stabilisation and growth".
Estonia is regarded as one of the keenest reformers amongst the states of theformer Soviet Union, with an open economy and wide-ranging privatisation of state industries.
Final GDP figures for 1996 have not been yet released but the economy rose by 3.5 percent over the first nine months of last year. Inflation last year was 14.8 percent.
Other goals listed by Vaehi included membership of the European Union in its next round of expansion.
He said he wanted to cut the corporate tax rate to 18 percent from January 1 1998.
Other areas the government viewed as important were its plans to reform the social insurance and pension system, Vaehi added.
